stem: A 10-year-old child has ADHD with prominent aggression affecting home and school life; which medication group is specifically noted as potentially helpful for aggression?

options.text: No medication is noted to help aggression

explanation: Clonidine or guanfacine are the medications specifically noted as potentially helpful for aggression in a child with ADHD.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 85

optionExplanations.A: Correct because clonidine and guanfacine are specifically linked to helping aggression.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because melatonin is used for sleep, and dexamphetamine is not specifically noted as helpful for aggression.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because atomoxetine and methylphenidate are ADHD treatments, but they are not the medication group specifically noted for aggression.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because these are long-acting stimulant formulations and are not specifically noted to reduce aggression.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the notes do mention clonidine or guanfacine as potentially helpful for aggression.
